terms.meaning: Two or more substances mixed without reacting, each keeping its own properties.
A substance made of only one kind of particle.
A simplest substance that cannot be broken down further into simpler substances.
Two or more elements combined chemically in a fixed ratio, with new properties.
A uniform mixture of metals, or of a metal and a non-metal.
An element with properties in between those of metals and non-metals.
A natural solid on the Earth, with a fixed chemical composition.

items.name: Non-uniform mixture
items.formula: The parts are not evenly spread and can often be told apart.
items.example: Sprout salad, or sand in water.

items.name: Uniform mixture
items.formula: The parts are evenly spread throughout.
items.example: Salt in water, air, and alloys.

items.name: Air is a mixture
items.formula: About 78% nitrogen, along with oxygen, argon, carbon dioxide and water vapour.
items.example: It looks the same throughout, so it is a uniform mixture.

items.name: Brass
items.example: A shiny alloy used for vessels.

items.name: Stainless steel
items.example: It resists rust better than iron does.

items.name: States of elements at room temperature
items.formula: Most are solids, 11 are gases and only 2 are liquids: mercury and bromine.
items.example: There are 118 known elements, so 118 − 11 − 2 = 105 are solids.

items.name: Examples of metalloids
items.example: Neither is fully a metal or fully a non-metal.

items.name: Molecules of an element
items.formula: In some gases, two atoms join as a molecule.
items.example: Hydrogen is H₂, and oxygen is O₂.

items.name: Splitting water with electricity
items.example: Hydrogen burns with a pop sound. Oxygen makes a flame brighter.

items.name: Heating sugar
items.formula: It breaks into black carbon and water, so sugar is a compound.
items.example: This is why overheated sugar turns black.

items.name: Iron and sulfur as a mixture
items.formula: A magnet pulls out the iron. Dilute acid gives hydrogen, with a pop sound.
items.example: The yellow and black parts can both be seen.

items.name: Iron sulfide as a compound
items.formula: A magnet has no effect. Dilute acid gives a gas that smells of rotten eggs.
items.example: Heating iron and sulfur together forms this new substance.

items.name: Kinds of minerals
items.formula: Most are compounds, such as quartz and mica. A few are pure elements, such as gold.

mistakes.text: Things sold as "pure", such as milk or honey, are mixtures in science.
A compound has new properties and a fixed ratio. A mixture keeps the old ones, in any ratio.
Air is not a pure substance, though it looks the same everywhere. It is a uniform mixture.
